claims.claim: MLflow 3.16: default local tracking URI is sqlite:///<cwd>/mlflow.db; params come back as strings; re-logging a param with a new value raises MlflowException; log_model accepts name=; sklearn models are saved as model.skops with requirements.txt, conda.yaml and python_env.yaml.
claims.source: Run with MLflow 3.16.1 in a scratch environment for this repository.

concept_html:
After twenty experiments nobody remembers which settings produced the good score. MLflow tracking records each run: parameters, metrics, tags and files. Examples use MLflow 3.16. On Databricks the tracking server is built in. Locally, MLflow 3 stores runs in a SQLite file, mlflow.db, in the working directory by default.

import mlflow

mlflow.set_experiment("churn")
with mlflow.start_run(run_name="lr-c1"):
    mlflow.log_params({"C": 1.0, "seed": 7, "features": "v3"})
    mlflow.set_tags({"git_commit": commit, "input_sha256": data_hash})
    model = train(X_train, y_train, C=1.0, seed=7)
    mlflow.log_metric("cv_auc", cv_auc)
    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, name="model", input_example=X_train[:5])

What to record, every time:

  • Parameters: every setting that changes the result, including the seed and the feature set version. MLflow stores them as strings: 1.0 comes back as '1.0'. A parameter cannot be changed once logged in a run. Logging C twice with different values raises MlflowException.
  • Tags: the Git commit and the input data hash from the run manifest (lesson B6-L2). They link the run to exact code and data.
  • Metrics: the honest estimate (lesson B11-L3) and its spread, named consistently across runs: cv_auc_mean, cv_auc_std.
  • The model: log_model saves the fitted object with a requirements.txt, conda.yaml and python_env.yaml pinned to the versions used. For scikit-learn models MLflow 3.16 saves in the skops format.

Use the with mlflow.start_run(): block. If training raises, the run ends with status FAILED instead of staying open and collecting the next run's metrics.

Compare runs with mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["churn"]), which returns a pandas DataFrame with params.*, metrics.* and tags.* columns.

def tracked_fit(X_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray, c: float, seed: int, commit: str, data_hash: str, cv_auc: float) -> str:
"""Fit and log one run. Returns the run ID."""
with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"lr-c{c}") as run:
mlflow.log_params({"C": c, "seed": seed})
mlflow.set_tags({"git_commit": commit, "input_sha256": data_hash})
model = LogisticRegression(C=c, random_state=seed, max_iter=1000).fit(X_train, y_train)
mlflow.log_metric("cv_auc", cv_auc)
mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, name="model", input_example=X_train[:5])
return run.info.run_id

import mlflow
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression


def tracked_fit(X_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray, c: float, seed: int, commit: str, data_hash: str, cv_auc: float) -> str:
    """Fit a logistic regression and record the run in MLflow.

    Returns:
        The MLflow run ID.
    """
    with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"lr-c{c}") as run:
        mlflow.log_params({"C": c, "seed": seed})
        mlflow.set_tags({"git_commit": commit, "input_sha256": data_hash})
        model = LogisticRegression(C=c, random_state=seed, max_iter=1000).fit(X_train, y_train)
        mlflow.log_metric("cv_auc", cv_auc)
        mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, name="model")
        return run.info.run_id

title: Track every run with MLflow
why_html: A model with AUC 0.83 went to production from a notebook. Three months later it needed retraining. Nobody could reproduce 0.83: the notebook had been edited since, the seed had not been recorded, and the training extract had been refreshed. The team spent two weeks rebuilding a model they had already built once. One tracked run with parameters, commit and data hash would have made the retrain a single command.
